claim: For every odd integer \(p\ge3\) and every real linear operator \(T:\ell_p^2\to\ell_p^2\) that is not a scalar multiple of an isometry, the norm-attainment set \(M_T=\{x\in S_{\ell_p^2}:\|Tx\|_p=\|T\|\}\) has at most \(4(p-1)\) points. The bound follows by partitioning projective directions at the coordinate axes and the kernels of the two rows of \(T\); on each of at most four sign sectors the norm-attainment equation is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most \(p\), and every maximizing root has multiplicity at least two. This strictly improves the earlier general estimate \(2(8p-5)\) for odd \(p\), without asserting that the new bound is optimal.

integrity.proof_basis: self-contained symbolic sign-sector and polynomial-root argument

scientific_limitations: The upper bound is not claimed optimal.
The result covers real two-dimensional spaces \(\ell_p^2\) only for odd integer \(p\ge3\).
No equality classification or exact maximum cardinality is established.
title: A sign-cell bound for norm attainment on odd-exponent Banach planes
